newsitem.title: USA: New Jersey men sentenced for 1989 sexual attack.
newsitem.headline: New Jersey men sentenced for 1989 sexual attack.

text.p: Three former high school athletes convicted of sexually assaulting a mentally retarded girl with a broom and a baseball bat were sent to prison Monday after years of battling their convictions.

The men, now in their mid-20s, were high school athletes in 1989 when they lured their victim to a basement in the upper-middle-class town of Glen Ridge, New Jersey, and sexually assaulted her as up to 10 schoolmates watched.
Although convicted in 1993, they have been free on bail while the case was appealed.
Monday's sentencing followed an appeals court decision last month that overturned the most serious charge against them, but left lesser charges intact.

Christopher Archer, 25, and Kevin Scherzer, 26, were sentenced to up to 15 years in a youth facility, which would likely bring their release in two to three years. Scherzer's twin brother, Kyle, received a seven-year sentence and could be free in 10 months.
Only Archer spoke in court before Judge Benjamin Cohen.

"I am truly sorry for what I have done to the family of (the victim) ... and also what I have done to my family," he said. "I know I can't undo what I have done, but I want to say again that I am truly sorry."
The three men were led from the crowded courtroom in handcuffs. All three have graduated from college and found jobs.

"Overall, I am pleased with the sentence. After eight years these defendants are finally going to jail, where they belong," said John Salerno, head of the state chapter of the American Association of Retarded Citizens. "This will send a message to predators throughout the country that they cannot prey on helpless citizens."

Bear Atwood of New Jersey's National Organisation for Women said: "I'm glad they're finally going to jail for what they did. I hope this is a message, especially to young athletes, that they can't do these sorts of things with women."
The crime attracted national attention, particularly after the trial judge originally handed down relatively light sentences and allowed the men to remain free on bail.

In tossing out the stiffest charge last month, the New Jersey appeals court found that the victim complied with the sexual act, thus eliminating the charge of first-degree aggravated sexual assault. But the court upheld the men's conviction on second-degree conspiracy to commit aggravated assault.
